newsitem.title: USA: Bonds part of incentive for new Ind. steel plant.
newsitem.headline: Bonds part of incentive for new Ind. steel plant.

text.p: - Several municipal bond issues may be sold in connection with a new steel plant AK Steel Holding Corp plans to build in Indiana, an attorney working on the project said Friday.
Thomas Downs, an attorney at Ice Miller Donadio & Ryan, said Friday that local governments, as well as Spencer County, where the plant is to be located, may issue bonds related to the project.

Downs, who worked with the local governments on an incentive package for the steel company and whose firm will serve as bond counsel on the issues, said Spencer County may sell tax increment financing bonds for the project.

In addition, sewer and water revenue bonds may be sold by municipalities near the plant site, he said. Those communities are Rockport, Grandview and Chrisney. Another water issue could be sold by a new regional water district.
Another possible target for bonding is qualified solid waste portions of the $1.1 billion steel plant itself, Downs said.
AK Steel announced Thursday it planned to build a carbon and stainless flat-rolled steel process complex near Rockport.
The state is providing $12.7 million in financial support for the plant, which will create 410 new jobs.
